props.name: three-component zinc-chromium-copper oxide catalyst (Cr/Zn=0.49, Cu/Zn=0.16 atom ratios)
approximate activation energy 15 kcal/mol
props.statement: An approximate activation energy of the methanol synthesis of 15 kcal/mol is found from the Arrhenius plot of the rate constants obtained along the bed.

props.name: activity falls after heating and after use
props.statement: The activity is high immediately after reduction of the raw catalyst at 250 °C and becomes lower after heating at 360 and 450 °C for two hours; the activity after synthesis runs 1-10 lies even lower than after heating at 450 °C.

props.name: axial temperature and concentration profiles
props.statement: The bed temperature remains below the oil bath temperature in the top zone, rises rapidly in the intermediate zone and, after a maximum, decreases slowly in the bottom zone; the methanol concentration is extremely low in the top zone, begins to rise in the intermediate zone and rises more slowly until the equilibrium concentration is attained at the bottom of the bed.

props.name: calculated profiles almost consistent
props.statement: Calculated average-temperature profiles for Exps. 1, 7 and 9 are almost, though not entirely, consistent with the experimental ones, which may be the order of accuracy to be expected of the performance data; calculated radial profiles agree well near the top of the third step, with a discrepancy increasing with bed length.

props.name: earlier reaction-heat formulae do not fit
props.statement: None of the earlier formulae for the axial reaction-heat distribution (Q = q0 e^-cx, Q = A e^-cx + B, Q = c1 e^-Mx + c2 e^-Nx) could express the present axial distribution data of the reaction heat.

props.name: start-up ignition risk
props.statement: Particularly at the beginning of the synthesis, a sudden temperature rise in the catalyst bed must be avoided because it would cause ignition of the catalyst granules.

props.name: outer tube surface resistance largest
props.statement: The heat transfer resistance is largest at the outer tube surface.

props.name: product impurities small
props.statement: The synthesis product contains only 1-3% water and 0-0.3% methyl formate as impurities; very little carbon dioxide or methane was detected in the exit gas.

props.name: radial temperature rise grows as H2/CO falls
props.statement: The radial temperature profile is concave upwards at the top of the bed, flat in the intermediate zone and convex upwards in the lower zone; the temperature rise over a cross section reaches about 40 °C in the bottom zone, and within the range of operating conditions its magnitude increases with a decreasing ratio of hydrogen to carbon monoxide.

props.name: STY rises with flow rate and with lower H2/CO
props.statement: The space-time yield of the reactor is rather lower than usual with commercial reactors; it becomes higher as the flow rate of the inlet gas is increased or as the ratio of hydrogen to carbon monoxide is decreased.

props.name: improve outer heat transfer and control temperature rise
props.statement: For efficient reactor performance, not only should the heat transfer at the outer tube surface be improved, but the temperature rise in the catalyst bed should also be controlled by a suitable means.

props.name: top zone too cold, bottom zone too hot
props.statement: Compared with the maximum-rate curve, the temperature in the top zone of the catalyst bed (low methanol concentration) is too low and that in the bottom zone (high methanol concentration) too high for efficient performance of the reactor.

props.name: tubular methanol synthesis reactor in a flowing hot-oil (Kanechlol) bath (Fig. 2)
props.description: Chromium steel (13% Cr) tube placed coaxially in a 300 mm cylinder; the heat-transfer medium Kanechlol flows upward through the annulus. Catalyst bed 950 mm high between 350 and 1300 mm from the bottom, with 1 l of copper granules above it. Three stainless-steel thermocouple protection tubes run through the bed (a center tube 8 mm o.d., 2 mm thick; two off-center tubes 5 mm o.d., 1 mm thick, 13 mm and 22 mm from the axis) with movable thermocouples for axial scans. Five copper sampling tubes (2 mm o.d., 0.5 mm thick) withdraw fluid at 150, 300, 450, 600 and 750 mm above the bed bottom at 30 l/hr each, through small coolers and 50 cc separators; a further sample is taken from the outlet.
